_note: Safe-food guide for caretakers and pet owners. Answers come only from this list; anything not listed is 'ask a vet'. Status: drafted from the sources; awaiting partner vet review.

_sources.ASPCA: ASPCA Animal Poison Control, People foods to avoid feeding pets: https://www.aspca.org/pet-care/aspca-poison-control/people-foods-avoid-feeding-your-pets
_sources.DAHD: Dept. of Animal Husbandry & Dairying: https://dahd.gov.in

dog.title: Feeding a street or pet dog
lines: Plain rice or roti with dal, curd, or a cooked egg or cooked meat, once or twice a day.
Clean water every day, in a clean bowl.
Feed at the same place and time, away from the road so dogs don't run into traffic.
No spicy, salty or sweet leftovers.

puppy.title: Feeding puppies
lines: 3–4 small soft meals a day: rice with curd, mashed dal, or cooked egg.
Ask a vet about deworming and vaccines (rabies and the core puppy vaccines).

cat.title: Feeding cats
lines: Cooked fish or chicken without bones, cooked egg, a little rice.
Milk is not needed; many adult cats get loose motions from it.

cow.title: Feeding cows
lines: Green fodder, dry fodder (straw) and clean water.
Fruit and vegetable peels are fine in small amounts, never in plastic bags.
Too many rotis, bread or sweets can upset a cow's stomach.

foods.why: Chocolate is poisonous to dogs and cats.
Grapes and raisins can damage a dog's kidneys.
Onion and garlic damage red blood cells in dogs and cats.
Cooked bones splinter and can tear the gut.
Many adult dogs and cats can't digest milk well and get loose motions; curd is usually easier.
Plain curd is usually easy on the stomach in small amounts.
Plain roti is fine for dogs; for cows, a few are fine but too many upset the stomach.
A little plain bread is okay, but it has little nutrition and too much upsets the stomach.
Plain cooked rice is a good base, with dal, curd or egg.
Cooked eggs are good protein. Don't feed raw eggs.
Sweet biscuits have sugar and little nutrition; fine as a rare treat, not a meal.
Sweets and sugar-free sweets (xylitol) are harmful; xylitol is poisonous to dogs.
Never feed food in plastic bags: animals swallow the plastic.
Spicy, salty and oily food upsets their stomachs.
Cooked fish without bones is good food.
Fruit and vegetable peels are fine for cows in small amounts, never in plastic bags.
Green and dry fodder are a cow's main food.
